messages.subject: Stan/Bayesian (alternative to) Scott-Knott (mean grouping) test?
parts:
I wonder if there is something similar to a Bayesian variant of a Scott-Knott test (which can be used to group treatments based on differences between their means rather than doing multiple pair-wise comparisons, e.g. http://www.scielo.br/scielo.php?script=sci_arttext&pid=S2179-84512014000100002 ) and if someone has used it in Stan?

I have ~20 treatments with 100+ measurements from each and they seem to be roughly log-normal distributed (measurements cannot be below 0) and I want to group the treatments in groups within which it is hard to tell a difference between treatments while the between-group differences are larger/significant. The Scott-Knott does not seem a good alternative here since the mean is not robust to a few outliers. I guess I can log-transform and then apply Scott-Knott but a bayesian treatment seems more useful.

Pointers/helpers appreciated, thanks.

Regards,

Robert Feldt

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Stan/Bayesian (alternative to) Scott-Knott (mean grouping) test?
parts:
Andrew may want to weigh in on this one, but you can start here:

http://andrewgelman.com/2013/08/20/correcting-for-multiple-comparisons-in-a-bayesian-regression-model/

We discuss K-means and LDA clustering in the manual, if you're more
concerned with the clustering than with hypothesis testing. But
the clustering analyses are typically very unstable in high dimensions.

- Bob
